purpose: Independent practice of A7.3 — translating one given core into two additional representations and recognizing the same core across different surfaces. Used as Lesson 3 consolidation and as evidence for the formative tracker.
student_learning_goal: I can show one pattern in three different ways.

parts.answer_key: Sound Parade: clap-stomp-clap-stomp-clap-stomp (or any valid AB sound pair, e.g., hum-tap-hum-tap-hum-tap). Body Parade: tall-small-tall-small-tall-small (or any valid AB body pair). Correct if (a) the same AB structure repeats, (b) the two surface elements differ. Accept any sound/body pair that holds the AB structure.

parts.answer_key: All three rows: YES (same core — all three are ABB). Core for animal row = Bea-Finn-Finn. Core for sound row = clap-stomp-stomp. Core for body row = tall-small-small. The structural core (ABB) is identical across all three; the surface elements change.

parts.answer_key: Any valid pattern where all three rows share the same structural core. A response is correct if (a) each row is a valid repeating pattern, (b) all three rows have the same core structure (e.g., all AB, or all ABB, or all ABC), and (c) the caption sentence is filled with a description of their core. Accept any core structure the child chooses.

early_finisher_prompt: Could you show your same core a fourth way? Try a colour pattern or a high-voice / low-voice pattern!
teacher_notes: Lesson 3 consolidation. Watch for the most common error: students changing the core when translating (e.g., AB animal → ABB sound). Part 1 is the most diagnostic: if a child fills the Sound row with claps and stomps but the count or order doesn't match the AB structure, the abstraction hasn't landed. Use Part 3 as evidence for the formative tracker columns 'Translates to sound version' and 'Translates to body version.' Children who succeed on Part 1 but fail Part 3 likely need more practice in concrete-to-abstract translation.
